[Gathered by ApprovalReady from official websites on 2026-10-12; a summary, not the source's wording] How to apply to Alice Springs Town Council for a development application.
Planning scheme: NT Planning Scheme 2020.
Lodge (online): Lodge with the NT Development Consent Authority on Development Applications Online (DAO) https://www.ntlis.nt.gov.au/planning/
Step 1: Check your zone and overlays on NR Maps, then check the NT Planning Scheme 2020 to see if your use is permitted, merit assessable or impact assessable.
Step 2: If you need a development permit, lodge on Development Applications Online (DAO) with a statement of effect and plans. The NT Government's Development Assessment Services processes it, not the council.
Step 3: Pay the NT Government application fee (from $269 for a single dwelling) and any advertising fee ($149).
Step 4: The council is asked to comment as a service authority. Some applications are exhibited for 7, 14 or 28 days.
Step 5: The Development Consent Authority decides. It takes about 8 weeks. Then get a building permit from a registered building certifier.
Pre-lodgement meetings: offered (Meet with an NT Government planner before you lodge. The council can advise on its own works and service requirements.).
Phone: (08) 8950 0500
Email: astc@astc.nt.gov.au
Address: 93 Todd Street, Alice Springs NT 0870
Planning enquiries email: astc@astc.nt.gov.au
Fee (2026-27): Development permit, single dwelling on one lot: $269 (NT Government fee, not council)
Fee (2026-27): Development permit, cost $100,001 to $250,000: $810
Fee (2026-27): Change of use, no physical development: $290
Fee (2026-27): Subdivision: $1,162 plus $56 per lot
Fee (2026-27): Advertising (exhibition): $149 (Per exhibition period, if needed)
references.interpretation: Check each line against the source pages (this council's documents) and correct nt_councils.json if anything is wrong before verifying. Gaps found: Development applications go to the NT Development Consent Authority, not the council. No separate planning email; the general council email is used for council matters like driveways, verges and rates. Council's role is as a service authority: it comments on development applications to the Development Consent Authority and approves works on council roads and drains. Its own planning page wasn't read. Spatial name is the upper-cased abb_name from the national Geoscape LGA layer (built from NT Government data). The NT Government's own LGA boundaries layer wasn't opened, so the spelling isn't confirmed there.

[Gathered by ApprovalReady from official websites on 2026-10-12; a summary, not the source's wording] How to apply to Tiwi Islands Regional Council for a development application.
Planning scheme: NT Planning Scheme 2020.
Lodge (online): Lodge with the NT Development Consent Authority on Development Applications Online (DAO) https://www.ntlis.nt.gov.au/planning/
Step 1: Check your zone and overlays on NR Maps, then check the NT Planning Scheme 2020 to see if your use is permitted, merit assessable or impact assessable.
Step 2: If you need a development permit, lodge on Development Applications Online (DAO) with a statement of effect and plans. The NT Government's Development Assessment Services processes it, not the council.
Step 3: Pay the NT Government application fee (from $269 for a single dwelling) and any advertising fee ($149).
Step 4: The council is asked to comment as a service authority. Some applications are exhibited for 7, 14 or 28 days.
Step 5: The Development Consent Authority decides. It takes about 8 weeks. Then get a building permit from a registered building certifier.
Pre-lodgement meetings: offered (Meet with an NT Government planner before you lodge. The council can advise on its own works and service requirements.).
Phone: (08) 8970 9500
Email: info@tiwiislands.nt.gov.au
Planning enquiries email: info@tiwiislands.nt.gov.au
Fee (2026-27): Development permit, single dwelling on one lot: $269 (NT Government fee, not council)
Fee (2026-27): Development permit, cost $100,001 to $250,000: $810
Fee (2026-27): Change of use, no physical development: $290
Fee (2026-27): Subdivision: $1,162 plus $56 per lot
Fee (2026-27): Advertising (exhibition): $149 (Per exhibition period, if needed)
